summary: Confirmed DONE. Commit 8fb94df00 swapped the per-snapshot, per-event and per-history-page TextEncoder.encode(JSON.stringify(value)) for approximateJsonSize, a walker that adds up string lengths. Live events are now sized per written row: an O(1) text.length for streaming deltas, a walk of the single activity or plan for upserts, and nothing for other events. evictToCapacity runs once per delivered chunk through a microtask. All 3 old estimator call sites and every per-event evictToCapacity call were converted. I benchmarked real 150-activity plus 150-message windows from the user's state.sqlite (161-319 KB, full payloads, so heavier than the web's preview payloads). The walk took 0.057-0.070 ms against 0.46-0.98 ms for the old stringify plus encode, 7-17x cheaper and below the windows' JSON.parse time (~0.26-0.33 ms). wsTransport hands each chunk to the listener synchronously, so the microtask coalescing really does run eviction once per chunk. Tests cover a pinned thread streaming past the budget and an activity updated in place being counted once. I found no other code path that re-serializes thread snapshots or events just to measure them. recordWebPerfPayload is behind the perf-profile flag. The remaining stringify sizers (sourceControlAtoms estimatePayloadBytes, workspaceMetadataPayloadBytes, hosted read vault encryption) sit outside this path or need the bytes anyway.

evidence.note: Walker: string.length+2, small constants for number, boolean and null, key length plus 4 per key. It builds no serialized string or Uint8Array, caps depth at 64 and keeps a cycle-guard Set.
estimateJsonLength = approximateJsonSize. git grep finds no TextEncoder or JSON.stringify left in the supervisor.

retainedRowWrite: streaming message-sent costs text.length only (matches mergeMessageUpdate's append at state/threads/store.ts:1663-1670). Activity and plan upserts walk the one row. Every other event type returns null.
recordRetainedSnapshot walks the snapshot once. recordRetainedEvent applies a per-row delta through rowRetainedBytes. recordRetainedHistoryPage walks page.items.
applyEvent calls scheduleEvictToCapacity, not evictToCapacity, for each event.

evictToCapacity (at most 32 entries) is coalesced by scheduleEvictToCapacity into one microtask after the chunk. It runs synchronously only after snapshots (586, 665) and stale recovery (517). The history-page apply at 496 also uses the scheduled path.
The companion per-event reconcileForEnvironment timer re-arm is coalesced the same way, once per chunk.
Stream.runForEachArray hands each server chunk to the listener in one synchronous loop, so the microtask really fires once per chunk.
planEvictionsToCapacity returns early when under both caps.
Tests cover a pinned thread streaming past the byte budget without evicting idle ones, and an in-place activity update counted once.
Micro-benchmark added alongside the fix. I measured separately on real DB windows (161-319 KB): walk 0.06 ms vs old 0.46-0.98 ms.

fixDefects: No correctness defects. Two caveats, neither worth reopening. (1) The walker's cost scales with object count, not bytes, and its per-object cost (closure recursion, for...in plus hasOwn, Set.add) is higher than stringify's. A synthetic payload of about 100k tiny objects (3.5 MB) took 7.3 ms against 6.0 ms for the old stringify plus encode. Real windows hold about 700-800 objects, the web requests 'preview' payloads (capped strings and arrays), and the most object-dense real activity has about 1.4k braces, so this does not happen in practice. (2) The 'seen' Set dedupes shared (non-cyclic) references as well as cycles, so a shared subtree is counted once. Decoded wire data is a fresh tree, so this changes nothing.
implementationSketch: None required. Optional micro-polish only: in approximateJsonSize.ts, drop the Set and rely on MAX_DEPTH (decoded wire data is acyclic), or swap for...in/hasOwn for Object.keys, to cut per-object cost on object-dense payloads. Check with scripts/perf/micro/client-retained-size.ts plus an object-dense fixture in approximateJsonSize.test.ts.
decisionReason: Client-runtime bookkeeping only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol impact.
